chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.html:
Today, the first visit to your property takes place on a screen. Quality photos and marketing determine who makes an appointment - and who moves on. Marketing is not a luxury: it’s what fills your visits.

This guide covers photos, video, description and delivery, to maximize attention and attract the right buyers.

Each chapter ends with a lined “My Notes” page.

Today, a sale is first won online: photos, video, description and distribution decide whether the buyer clicks or passes. This guide covers every marketing lever, from preparing locations to distributing to the right audience.

The principle: take care of the digital showcase as much as the property itself.

chapters.title: Photos: your digital showcase
chapters.objective: Understand why photos make (or break) the sale.
chapters.html:
Understand why photos make (or break) the sale.

Buyers judge your property in seconds based on photos. Bright, sharp, well-framed images generate more clicks, more visits and better deals. Dark or amateur photos do the opposite, even for a beautiful property.

  • Professional photos: light, controlled wide-angle, prepared property (staging).
  • Logical order and strong main photo (often the facade or the featured piece).
  • Sufficient number: show all the key parts without misleading.

Buyers judge in a few seconds, on the photos, before even reading the description. Professional, bright and well-framed photos make the difference between “we visit” and “we pass”. It is the most profitable marketing investment in a sale.

Emilie's advice

Never skimp on photos: it's the investment with the best return of the entire sale. A property that is well prepared and poorly photographed sells less well than it should.

chapters.title: Video and virtual tour
chapters.objective: Go beyond the photo to stand out.
chapters.html:
Go beyond the photo to stand out.

Video and virtual tours (3D tours, plans) allow buyers to plan ahead before traveling. They attract serious buyers, including those from further afield, and filter out less relevant visits.

  • Short and dynamic video highlighting the route and the atmosphere.
  • Virtual tour to explore at your own pace.
  • Layout plan to understand the volumes.

Video and virtual tours (3D, plans) allow buyers to plan and filter before traveling: you receive more qualified visitors. For out-of-area buyers, this is often what triggers the first in-person visit.

Emilie's advice

The video tells the atmosphere and the way of life that a photo captures. For a property with strong character (view, layout, area), it is a powerful trigger for emotion and visits.

chapters.title: The description that makes you want
chapters.objective: Write text that sells without misleading.
chapters.html:
Write text that sells without misleading.

  • Open on asset no. 1 (location, light, renovation, courtyard).
  • Describe the spaces concretely and the benefits (not just dimensions).
  • Mention the neighborhood and its amenities.
  • Stay honest: A misleading description creates disappointed visits and failed deals.

A good description opens with asset no. 1 (location, light, renovation, courtyard), describes concretely without exaggeration, and ends with a call to action. It sells without deceiving: promising what you don't deliver generates disappointed visits and offers that fall through.

Emilie's advice

Sell the benefits, not just the features: not “12-foot kitchen”, but “a kitchen bathed in light, designed for entertaining”. The buyer is buying a life, not dimensions.

chapters.title: Distribution: being seen by the right buyers
chapters.objective: Maximize exposure to the right audience.
chapters.html:
Maximize exposure to the right audience.

  • Wide distribution: Centris, portals, social networks, network of brokers.
  • Targeting: put the property in front of active buyers in the area.
  • Timing of the launch: concentrate exposure on the first weeks, when interest is maximum.
  • Signs, open houses and QR codes to also attract local buyers.

Much of the value of a broker lies in this network and this diffusion machine, which are difficult to replicate alone.

Dissemination must be broad AND fair: Centris, portals, social networks, network of contacts and buyers. A beautiful property that is poorly advertised sells poorly; exposure to the right audience is as important as the quality of the visuals.

Emilie's advice

Take care of the launch: concentrate marketing energy on the first two weeks. This is the window where interest is strongest and where your best deals are often played out.

chapters.title: Before the camera: prepare the scene
chapters.html:
Great photos start with preparation.

The best photos don't make up for a poorly prepared property. Before the session:

  • Declutter and put each piece away.
  • Clean thoroughly (surfaces, windows, floors).
  • Maximize light : curtains open, light bulbs on.
  • Store objects personal and everyday signs (dishes, products).
  • Heal theexterior and the entry for the first photo.

An impeccable property produces images that make you want to visit - and that's the whole point.

The best photos don't make up for a poorly prepared property: declutter, clean thoroughly, maximize light and put away personal items BEFORE the session. Treat photo day like a visit from a discerning buyer - it's your first impression online, and there's only one.

Emilie's advice

Treat photo day like a demanding buyer's visit: everything must be tidy, clean and bright. Photos are your first impression online, and there's only one.

chapters.title: Action plan
chapters.html:
Your next steps, concretely.

This week

  1. Prepare the property for professional photos.
  2. Decide if a video/virtual tour is appropriate.

Within 30 days

  1. Write a profit-oriented and honest description.
  2. Plan a wide distribution and a concentrated launch.

Then

  1. Measure interest (clicks, visits) and adjust as needed.

Before posting online

  1. Prepare the locations, then plan professional photos (and video).
  2. Write a description that opens with asset no. 1 and plan wide distribution.

chapters.title: Resources & glossary
chapters.html:
• Professional photos: bright and clear images, prepared by staging.
  • Virtual tour: remote 3D exploration of the property.
  • Profit-oriented description: text that sells a way of life, honestly.
  • Distribution: Centris, portals, social networks, broker network.
  • Launch momentum: concentration of the exhibition in the first weeks.
  • Centris: reference platform for properties for sale in Quebec.
  • Virtual tour: 3D tour allowing you to visit remotely.
  • Digital curb appeal: quality of photos that makes you want to visit.
  • Call to action: clear invitation to visit or make an offer.
  • Diffusion: exposure of the ad to the right audience of buyers.
